turns: Brainstorm 10 app ideas for hobbyist 3D printer owners.

rubric.text: The ideas are genuinely distinct (no two are minor variations of the same app).
Each idea is tied to a specific problem hobbyists actually have (failed prints, filament tracking, calibration, finding models, etc.).
At least three ideas go beyond the obvious (a model marketplace, a basic slicer) or put a fresh angle on them.
Each idea is described briefly enough to scan the list quickly.

turns: I have one weekend and know React and Supabase. Give me app ideas I could actually ship by Sunday night, then pick the best one and outline the build plan.

rubric.text: Ideas are realistically shippable in a weekend by one person.
Plans use React and Supabase (auth, database, storage, edge functions as relevant).
Picks one idea and gives a concrete reason.
The build plan is time-boxed (e.g. Saturday morning/afternoon, Sunday) with an explicit MVP cut line.

notes: 'What if' + 'kick around' route to Carson + Dali in Prism.
turns: What if we made a to-do app that deletes tasks you haven't done in 7 days? Kick this idea around with me.

rubric.text: Engages with this specific idea (forced prioritisation, fresh start) rather than generic to-do app advice.
Names real downsides (anxiety, losing important tasks, users gaming it) honestly.
Proposes concrete variants or mitigations (archive instead of delete, warnings before deletion, a 'still relevant?' prompt).
Identifies who would want this.
Keeps it conversational, ending with a question or next step for the user, as 'kick this around with me' implies.

turns: Brainstorm ways to monetize a free habit-tracking app without showing ads.

rubric.text: Options are concrete and distinct (e.g. premium tier, one-time unlock, coaching, team/B2B plans, themes/content).
Notes tradeoffs or which options fit a small team best.
Does not suggest selling user data, or explicitly warns against it.

notes: Prism's flagship 'war room' (all personas, Susie moderates). Baseline gets the same words.
turns: War room: should my two-person startup build a mobile app or a web app first? We're making a tool for landscapers to send quotes to customers.

rubric.text: Reasons from the landscapers' actual context (quoting on site from a phone, office work at a desk, how customers receive quotes).
Reaches a clear recommendation (e.g. a mobile-friendly web app or PWA first) with reasons.
Suggests a cheap way to resolve the key uncertainty (e.g. talking to or watching a few landscapers) before building much.
Surfaces real tradeoffs (offline use, camera, app-store friction, development cost for two people) without padding or staged disagreement.

pairwise_focus: Which response would help a two-person team make the better first-platform decision?
